This traditional Middle Eastern feast is perfect for grand celebrations, offering a symphony of rich flavors and textures that will impress every guest. Its slow roasting process ensures unparalleled succulence and depth, making it an unforgettable culinary experience.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the lamb shoulder dry with paper towels. In a small bowl, combine olive oil, salt, black pepper, baharat, cumin, coriander, turmeric, paprika, and minced garlic to form a thick paste.

instructions.title: Marinate and Setup for Roasting
instructions.text: Rub the spice paste generously all over the lamb shoulder, ensuring it covers all surfaces. Place the quartered onions and lemon halves in a large, sturdy roasting pan. Add 2 cups of water or lamb broth to the bottom of the pan. Place the marinated lamb on top of the onions and lemon.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Cover the roasting pan tightly with heavy-duty foil, ensuring no steam escapes. Preheat your oven to 150C 300F. Roast the lamb for 4 to 5 hours, or until it is incredibly tender and easily pulls apart with a fork. For a slightly crisper exterior, remove the foil for the last 30 minutes of roasting.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice Base
instructions.text: While the lamb roasts, rinse the basmati rice thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the diced carrots and saute for 5 minutes until slightly softened. Add the frozen peas and cook for another 2 minutes. Remove the cooked vegetables from the pot and set aside.

instructions.title: Cook the Aromatic Rice
instructions.text: In the same pot, melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter. Add the rinsed rice, cinnamon sticks, crushed cardamom pods, and bay leaves. Stir for 2-3 minutes to lightly toast the rice and release the aromas. Pour in the 6 cups of lamb broth and add the golden raisins. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly with a lid, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and the rice is fluffy.

instructions.title: Assemble the Lamb Ouzi
instructions.text: Once the lamb is cooked, carefully remove it from the roasting pan and transfer it to a large cutting board. Using two forks, shred the tender meat off the bone. Discard any bones, excess fat, or skin. Fluff the cooked rice with a fork, then gently fold in the sauteed carrots and peas. Transfer the fragrant rice to a large, decorative serving platter.

instructions.title: Garnish and Serve
instructions.text: Arrange the shredded lamb generously over the bed of aromatic rice. Toast the pine nuts and sliced almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden brown, watching carefully to prevent burning. Garnish the Lamb Ouzi with the toasted nuts and freshly chopped parsley. Drizzle some of the flavorful lamb drippings from the roasting pan over the dish for extra moisture and taste. Serve immediately as a magnificent centerpiece.

tips: For truly tender lamb, ensure your roasting pan is tightly sealed with foil to trap steam, which helps break down the connective tissues during the long slow roast.
Baharat is crucial for authentic Ouzi flavor. If unavailable, a mix of allspice, black pepper, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cardamom can be a decent substitute.
Leftover Lamb Ouzi can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat gently, adding a splash of broth to the rice to maintain moisture.
article:
Unveiling a truly magnificent centerpiece for any celebratory gathering, Lamb Ouzi stands as a testament to the rich culinary traditions of the Middle East. This isn't just a meal; it's an experience, a slow-roasted masterpiece that fills your home with intoxicating aromas and your table with an unforgettable feast. If you're looking to impress guests or simply indulge in a deeply flavorful and tender lamb dish, mastering the art of Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi is a culinary journey well worth taking. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to create this show-stopping Middle Eastern dinner recipe, ensuring succulent lamb and perfectly spiced rice every time.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?
Lamb Ouzi, sometimes spelled "Ozzy" or "Ouzy," is a grand Middle Eastern dish renowned for its spectacular presentation and incredible flavor. At its heart is tender, slow-roasted lamb, often a whole leg or shoulder, cooked until it's falling off the bone. This succulent lamb is traditionally served atop a bed of fragrant, spiced basmati rice, which is usually studded with toasted nuts like pine nuts, almonds, and pistachios, along with dried fruits such as raisins or cranberries. While some variations involve stuffing the lamb with the rice mixture, the whole slow-roasted method focuses on the lamb's unadulterated tenderness, allowing its rich flavor to shine through before being generously piled onto the aromatic rice. It’s a dish synonymous with hospitality, special occasions, and family gatherings, representing generosity and culinary artistry.

## Ingredients for Lamb Ouzi
Creating an authentic Lamb Ouzi requires a thoughtful selection of ingredients, focusing on quality and aromatic spices. For the star of the show, you'll need:

**For the Lamb:**
*   A whole leg of lamb (bone-in, approximately 5-7 lbs / 2.3-3.2 kg) or a large lamb shoulder. Bone-in adds more flavor.
*   **Marinade:**
    *   Olive oil
    *   Garlic cloves, minced
    *   Lemon juice
    *   Ground cumin
    *   Ground coriander
    *   Smoked paprika
    *   Turmeric powder
    *   Black pepper
    *   Salt (sea salt or kosher salt)
    *   Optional: a pinch of ground cardamom, cinnamon, or a dash of allspice for deeper Middle Eastern notes.
    *   Optional aromatics: Fresh rosemary sprigs, bay leaves.

**For the Spiced Ouzi Rice:**
*   Basmati rice, rinsed thoroughly
*   Butter or ghee
*   Onion, finely chopped
*   Garlic cloves, minced
*   Chicken or lamb broth (or water)
*   Spices: Ground cinnamon, ground allspice, ground cardamom, salt, black pepper.
*   Toasted nuts for garnish: Pine nuts, slivered almonds, pistachios (a mix is ideal).
*   Optional additions: Raisins or dried cranberries, fresh parsley or mint for garnish.

Having these ingredients ready is the first step towards a successful Lamb Ouzi Recipe.

## How to Make Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi
Preparing this magnificent Lamb Ouzi Recipe involves a few key stages, each contributing to the final, mouth-watering result.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:** Pat the lamb dry. In a bowl, mix olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, salt, and pepper to form a paste. Score the lamb deeply in several places with a sharp knife, then rub the marinade all over, ensuring it gets into the scores. If possible, cover and refrigerate the lamb for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight, allowing the flavors to penetrate deeply. This lengthy marination is crucial for a flavorful Lamb Ouzi.

2.  **Slow Roasting the Lamb:** Preheat your oven to a low temperature, around 300°F (150°C). Place the marinated lamb in a large roasting pan. Pour about 1-2 cups of water or broth into the bottom of the pan to create a moist environment and prevent drying. Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil. This traps steam, ensuring the lamb cooks slowly and becomes incredibly tender. Roast for 4-6 hours, or until the internal temperature reaches 190-200°F (88-93°C) and the meat is fork-tender, practically falling off the bone. Baste occasionally with the pan juices. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and develop a beautiful crust. Once cooked, remove the lamb from the oven, cover loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes before carving or shredding. This resting period is vital for juicy meat.

3.  **Prepare the Spiced Ouzi Rice:** While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt butter or ghee over medium heat. Sauté the chopped onion until softened and translucent, then add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the ground cinnamon, allspice, cardamom, salt, and pepper, cooking for about 30 seconds until aromatic. Add the rinsed basmati rice and stir well to coat every grain with the spices. Pour in the chicken or lamb broth (or water), bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until all the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. Fluff with a fork.

4.  **Toast the Nuts:** In a small dry skillet, toast the pine nuts, almonds, and pistachios over medium-low heat until golden and fragrant. Watch them carefully as they can burn quickly.

## Tips for Perfect Slow Roasted Lamb
Achieving the perfect Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi requires patience and a few expert tricks:

*   **Marinate Generously:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the lamb sits in the spice mixture, the more flavor it will absorb, leading to a truly memorable Lamb Ouzi Recipe. Overnight is highly recommended.
*   **Low and Slow is Key:** Resist the urge to crank up the heat. A low oven temperature over many hours breaks down the tough connective tissues in the lamb, resulting in unparalleled tenderness.
*   **Keep it Moist:** Covering the roasting pan tightly with foil for most of the cooking time creates a steamy environment, preventing the lamb from drying out. Adding a little liquid to the pan also helps.
*   **Rest Your Meat:** This step is non-negotiable. Resting allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, ensuring every bite is succulent. Cutting into it too soon will result in dry lamb.
*   **Use a Meat Thermometer:** While fork-tenderness is a good indicator, a reliable meat thermometer ensures your lamb reaches the ideal internal temperature for fall-off-the-bone results (190-200°F / 88-93°C).
*   **Score the Lamb:** Scoring the surface of the lamb helps the marinade penetrate deeper and also allows the fat to render more evenly, creating a crispy exterior.

## Serving & Garnish Ideas
The presentation of Lamb Ouzi is almost as important as its taste. It’s a dish meant to be admired before it’s devoured.

*   **Grand Platter:** Traditionally, the beautifully tender lamb, either whole or artfully shredded/carved, is placed majestically on a large serving platter, surrounded by the fragrant spiced Ouzi rice.
*   **Toasted Nuts:** Liberally sprinkle the toasted pine nuts, slivered almonds, and pistachios over the entire dish. Their crunch and nutty flavor are essential.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A generous scattering of freshly chopped parsley or mint adds a burst of color and freshness that cuts through the richness of the lamb.
*   **Pomegranate Seeds:** For a vibrant pop of color and a tart counterpoint, scatter fresh pomegranate seeds over the top.
*   **Fried Onions:** Crispy fried onions can add another layer of texture and savory depth.
*   **Sides:** Serve with cooling accompaniments like a simple cucumber and tomato salad, a bowl of creamy labneh or plain yogurt, or a selection of Middle Eastern pickles. These sides provide a refreshing balance to the rich main course.

## Ouzi Recipe Variations & Substitutions
While the classic Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi Recipe is magnificent, there are several ways to adapt it to your preferences or available ingredients:

*   **Lamb Cut:** If a whole leg is too large, a bone-in lamb shoulder (picnic roast or Boston butt) works equally well and offers similar tenderness when slow-roasted. For smaller gatherings, a boneless lamb roast can be used, but adjust cooking times accordingly.
*   **Rice Spices:** Experiment with different spice blends. Some recipes include dried lime (loomi), bay leaves, or a touch of saffron for added complexity. A pre-made Middle Eastern seven-spice blend can also be a convenient substitute for individual spices.
*   **Dried Fruits:** While raisins are common, dried cranberries, apricots, or even chopped dates can be used in the rice for varying levels of sweetness and chewiness.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Some cooks add finely diced carrots or peas to the rice for extra color and nutrition.
*   **Individual Ouzi Parcels:** While not a whole slow roast, a popular variation involves cooking individual portions of spiced rice and lamb (or minced meat) wrapped in phyllo pastry or dough, baked until golden. This is a different style of Ouzi but shares the same core flavors.
*   **Pressure Cooker/Instant Pot:** For faster cooking, the lamb can be cooked in a pressure cooker until tender, then finished in the oven for browning. This significantly reduces the cooking time, though the slow-roasting method yields a unique depth of flavor and texture.

Embracing the Lamb Ouzi Recipe is an invitation to explore the heart of Middle Eastern cuisine. Its combination of tender, aromatic lamb and fragrant, spiced rice makes for a truly unforgettable meal, perfect for celebrating life's special moments. Whether you follow the traditional methods or explore creative variations, this dish promises to be a spectacular addition to your culinary repertoire.
